annotations.text:
Block Canvas - a shell for wiring blocks into runnable graphs.

Left: the library, categorised by what a block does. Centre: an infinite node canvas. Right: an inspector that reshapes itself around whatever is selected.

Top row is the same shell at three moments: nothing built, mid-wire, mid-run.
The right panel is the whole idea: five different selections, five different panels, one 328px column.
Every block declares typed ports. A wire is coloured by its data type, and the type is what makes a connection legal or refuses it mid-drag. Ten types, nine categories plus Custom.
One block, labelled, plus every run state - and the wiring rules. Handle wires (tools, memory) carry a two-way mark at the holder's end: the call goes out, the reply comes back.

Continuous running.

A graph with a source block (Senses: watch folder, webhook, schedule, webcam...) never finishes - it stays armed and every event runs downstream. The transport chip switches from Run to live, and the inspector with nothing selected becomes the run-mode panel.

A Loop is a dashed frame on the canvas: blocks inside repeat once per item.

The home assistant, as one graph. Left to right: senses feed specialist models, which feed an orchestrator LLM; memory stores bundle through a Memory hub the same way tools bundle through a Toolbox; the model's text goes to a display and a speaker, its thoughts to a terminal, and its actions to motors - via a tool call that warns first and then runs.

Feedback: the Motors block replies on its tool handle, streams its state into the orchestrator's context, and raises a fault on an exec port that pauses the Toolbox until you resume it.

Warn, never block: the user owns their tools. A truly dangerous action gets a prompt; the prompt always has a Continue.

Custom blocks.

Write code inline or point the block at a file it watches. The signature is the interface: parameters without defaults are input ports, parameters with defaults are settings, the return annotation is the output. Save it and it sits in the library like a built-in.

The code is one view of the block, not the block: compact, summary or code, per block. A big program lives in the drawer under the canvas, or in your own editor, while the block on the canvas stays small.
Click any block to watch the inspector swap. Press Run to put the graph in flight - wires animate, status dots turn green, the console reports.
